headline: Chips Carry the Day as Sellers Swamp Nearly Every Other Corner of the Market
body_html:
Friday's session closed with a markedly divided tape: semiconductors surged in near-isolation while decliners outnumbered advancers by a wide margin — 340 down against 204 up across a universe of 545 names. The chip complex served as the session's lone reliable shelter, posting a sector gain of roughly 2.5 percent even as six of the eight tracked sectors finished in the red, with homebuilders absorbing the sharpest punishment, off more than 1.6 percent.

Memory and equipment names led the advance with conviction. Sandisk topped the leaderboard, surging nearly 11 percent, while Lam Research and Applied Materials each climbed roughly 7 percent, and MaxLinear added more than 8 percent. Coherent and Seagate rounded out a top-six gainer list that was almost uniformly silicon. The cohesion of the move suggested investors were rotating into hard-infrastructure hardware rather than software, which slid more than 1 percent on the day.

On the other side of the ledger, steelmaker Nucor dropped more than 6 percent, and metallurgical coal producer Alpha Metallurgical Resources shed nearly as much — a signal that industrial commodity demand expectations softened into the weekend. The broader tone was defensive caution dressed up in one very bright chip-sector exception.

briefs.headline: Qualcomm Bucks Its Own Sector, Slides Nearly 6 Percent
briefs.body: While semiconductor equipment and memory names surged Friday, Qualcomm moved sharply in the opposite direction, falling 5.82 percent to rank among the session's steepest decliners. The divergence underscored that Friday's chip rally was selective — concentrated in storage, memory, and capital-equipment names rather than the broader semiconductor space.

briefs.headline: Wendy's Franchisee Seeks Bankruptcy Protection Amid Fast-Food Headwinds
briefs.body: A Wendy's franchisee filed for Chapter 11 protection Friday, adding pressure to a burger chain already navigating a difficult consumer environment. The filing highlights ongoing stress among quick-service restaurant operators as traffic trends remain challenged, even as McDonald's has drawn renewed attention from traders looking for value-oriented consumer plays.

briefs.headline: Disney Moves to Formalize Technology Leadership With First-Ever CTO Appointment
briefs.body: The media and entertainment giant named a chief technology officer for the first time in its history Friday, signaling an accelerating push to embed technology more deeply across its business. The appointment reflects a broader industry trend of legacy media companies restructuring executive ranks to compete with streaming-native and platform-first rivals.

briefs.headline: Nike Cuts Ties With Mbappé as On Running Claims Soccer's Biggest Signature
briefs.body: Nike ended its endorsement relationship with French football star Kylian Mbappé on Friday, with the athlete promptly signing with Swiss running-and-lifestyle brand On. The signing marks a significant coup for On's brand ambitions and a notable setback for Nike's effort to anchor its global football marketing around one of the sport's most recognized figures.

briefs.headline: Air France Leans Into Luxury to Cushion Ongoing Iran War Disruption
briefs.body: Air France is deepening its focus on premium and luxury cabin offerings as a hedge against the revenue volatility created by the ongoing Iran conflict, according to reports Friday. The carrier's strategy of targeting high-yield passengers — including premium food-and-beverage experiences — is helping offset route disruptions and softer economy-class demand.

briefs.headline: Geopolitical Tensions Remain Elevated as U.S. War Casualties Revised Higher
briefs.body: A Washington Post report cited by Reuters on Friday indicated that American troop deaths in the Iran conflict exceed previously released Pentagon figures by at least four. The disclosure adds to investor unease already visible in energy and materials sector weakness, while a senior Republican lawmaker pressed the administration to take a harder stance in concurrent negotiations with Beijing.
